rationale.conceptual: The method couples deep neural network interatomic potentials, ab initio data, phonon dispersion validation, equilibrium molecular dynamics with Green-Kubo thermal conductivity, and Green-Kubo modal analysis. While the components exist in prior literature, integrating them correctly requires genuine understanding of each part (especially the modal decomposition and the physics of thermal transport). The conceptual load is high, involving non-trivial physics and careful implementation of several interacting numerical methods.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of at least 7 stages (AIMD data generation, NNP training, phonon validation, size-convergence study, four-temperature EMD simulations with 15 independent runs each, supercell lattice dynamics, and GKMA) and depends on multiple external codes (deepmd-kit, LAMMPS, Alamode, possibly CP2K). Each stage has strict parameter requirements, long-running simulations, and handoffs between tools. Orchestrating this end-to-end is very complex and highly error-prone.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires reproducing a full pipeline: training a deep neural network interatomic potential using DeePot-SE on ab initio data, validating phonon dispersion, running equilibrium MD with Green-Kubo thermal conductivity calculations at multiple temperatures for an anisotropic crystal, and performing a Green-Kubo modal analysis. The underlying physics (NNP, Green-Kubo, modal decomposition) is advanced, and the pipeline is long and fragile with many specialized tools. The agent needs a GPU for training and production MD simulations; the dataset is small (~70 MB), and memory requirements are modest.
